albums.album: The Earth Is Not a Cold Dead Place
albums.blurb: Explosions in the Sky are a four-piece from Austin, Texas who have never used vocals: everything is built from two or three interlocking electric guitars, bass, and drums. This is their third album, released on Temporary Residence in November 2003, and the one that defined their sound — five long pieces that move in slow crescendos from chiming quiet to full-band peaks. It preceded, and led directly to, their score for the 2004 film Friday Night Lights, which made them the default sound of cinematic Americana.
albums.reception: Pitchfork's contemporary review called it "a sweetly melodic, inspirationally hopeful album for a genre whose trademark is tragedy," and it remains the band's best-known record.

albums.blurb: Bahamas is Afie Jurvanen, a Finnish-Canadian singer and guitarist who spent years as Feist's sideman before going solo. Earthtones, his fourth album (Brushfire, January 2018), is the point where his laid-back folk turned toward smooth soul and funk: he recorded it with bassist Pino Palladino and drummer James Gadson, the rhythm section of D'Angelo's Black Messiah, having written the songs with that pairing specifically in mind.
albums.reception: Earthtones won the 2019 Juno Award for Adult Alternative Album of the Year and was nominated for the Grammy for Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical.

albums.blurb: The Zombies' second and final 1960s album, recorded on a self-funded budget at Abbey Road and Olympic Studios in the summer of 1967 and released by CBS in April 1968 — by which point the band had already broken up. Rod Argent and Chris White wrote the songs around Mellotron, piano, and Colin Blunstone's breathy lead vocals, and the misspelled title came from the sleeve artist. Commercially invisible at release, it has since become one of the defining British baroque-pop records.
albums.reception: "Time of the Season" reached No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1969, more than a year after the album's release and after the band had split.
